nodes.name: A resubmitted request starts again at Project Manager confirmation.
One responsive web application serves all roles through role-specific screens; there is no separate native mobile or back-office application.
Admin and HR are treated as one actor, Admin/HR.
Requirement priorities were proposed during analysis; the URS states none.
The leave request status names (PENDING_CONFIRMATION, PENDING_APPROVAL, DENIED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) are proposed labels.
Sign-in and sign-out are handled by the company's single sign-on, so this system has no sign-in use case of its own.
A request can be reviewed at any time from submission up to the end of the month of the leave start date.
The managers who see leave reports are Line Managers. Project Managers have no access to reports.
'The last week' in the weekly notification is the week that ends on the Friday the notification is sent.
The base days and N (years of service per extra day) are configured per leave type by Admin/HR.
UC-006 keeps its ID but changes from an import by Admin/HR to an automatic annual refresh run by the system.
When a request skips confirmation (a Project Manager's own request, or an employee with no project), the Line Manager receives the email that confirmation would send.
Weekends are Saturday and Sunday in every country.
The company single sign-on supports OpenID Connect.
The system runs as containers on a Kubernetes platform chosen by the client, with managed PostgreSQL and S3-compatible object storage available.
Employee submits a leave request: leave type, dates with day part (All day, Morning, Afternoon), the confirming Project Manager and any required documents

System blocks a request with dates outside the allowed window, a missing required document or an ineligible leave type; it accepts a request that exceeds the entitlement, flags it for manual review, and emails the selected Project Manager

Selected Project Manager confirms or denies the request. The step is auto-confirmed when the requester is a Project Manager and skipped when the employee belongs to no project. Confirmation emails the Line Manager; denial emails the employee
Line Manager approves or rejects the request. The employee is emailed
After a denial or rejection, the employee may modify and resubmit the request
Until the Line Manager has approved it, the employee may cancel the request
When the month of the leave start date ends, the system cancels a request that is still not confirmed or approved
System starts the annual refresh automatically at the start of the year
System calculates each employee's entitlements for the new year: base days plus one day per N years of service, for the leave types the employee is eligible for
System checks the requests still pending against the new entitlements
Admin/HR creates or edits a leave type
Admin/HR sets its eligibility rule (gender) and its entitlement rule (base days, and N years of service per extra day)
System fetches check-in and check-out data from the card scanner system
System determines each employee's off-work days among the working days of the last week
System matches off-work days against the employee's leave requests; any submitted request counts
System notifies the employee of absent days without a leave request and absent days with a valid leave request
User chooses the level: unit, department or entire company. A Line Manager is limited to their own unit
System shows leave usage statistics for that level
Exceeding the entitlement is reviewed, not blocked
Reviewer dashboards show actionable requests by default
Employee selects the confirming Project Manager
Line Managers do not request leave
Master data comes from the HR system
No confirmation for an employee without a project

Which policy rules can a request violate and still be submitted (exceeding the entitlement, missing a required document, not eligible for the leave type)? Is the date window (future, or past within the current month) a hard block or also a reviewable violation?
What happens to a request that is not confirmed or approved by the end of the month of the leave start date? May a request for a later month be reviewed before that month starts?
Who confirms a request from an employee who belongs to no project?

Where do employees, the organisational structure, project teams, line-manager assignments and role assignments come from: an existing HR system, an import, or maintenance inside this system? How do country/city/office relate to unit/department?
How do users sign in: the company's single sign-on / identity provider, or accounts managed by this system?

For the entitlement import: what is the file format, and what does the annual refresh do to unused entitlement and to requests still pending? Does the system calculate seniority-based entitlement, or is it only imported? Do the rules differ per country?
Which days count as working days when leave is counted and when the weekly notification determines absences: do weekends and public holidays (which differ per country) count?
Can an employee cancel or withdraw a request, and in which statuses (pending, approved)?
Who approves a Line Manager's own request, and what happens when the Project Manager and the Line Manager of a request are the same person?
Are Admin and HR one role or two? Which managers see reports (Project Managers, Line Managers, both), and is what they see limited to their own unit, office or country?

For the weekly notification: which period does it cover, which days are working days (weekends, public holidays per country), and does a 'valid leave request' mean approved only or any submitted request?
How is card scanner data made available by the external system (API, file, database), how often, and which identifier links a scanner record to an employee?
Which mail service is used? What must be configurable in the notification emails, and by whom? Are emails also sent when a request is cancelled, by the employee or automatically?
Which languages are needed at launch, if any?
How is HR system data made available (API, file, database), and how often can it be fetched?
How does an employee who joins during the year get a leave entitlement?
What does the entitlement rule of a seniority-based leave type look like (for example: base days plus one day per N years of service)?
Where does the public holiday calendar of each country come from: the HR system, or maintained in this system by Admin/HR? Are weekends Saturday and Sunday in every country?
In which time zone are the current month, the end of the month and Friday evaluated: one company time zone, or the local time of each employee's office?

How are the documents a leave type can require defined: does Admin/HR type each document name on the leave type, or choose from a fixed list of document types kept elsewhere in system settings? If it is a fixed list, who maintains it?

When does a change to a leave type take effect? (a) Does changing the base days or the years of service per extra day recalculate the entitlements of the current year, or apply from the next annual refresh? (b) Do employees get an entitlement for a leave type created during the year, before the next refresh? (c) Are requests already submitted checked again when the gender eligibility or the required documents change?

Which limits apply to a leave type? Must the name be unique, and how long can it be? Which range can the base days take: can it be 0 or a half day, and is there a maximum? Does a leave type such as Unpaid Leave have no entitlement limit at all? Which range can N (years of service per extra day) take?
Which gender values does the HR system provide for an employee, and which eligibility options must a leave type offer: all employees, female only, male only, or others?

Does a reviewer give a reason when denying or rejecting a leave request: mandatory, optional or not at all? May a reviewer add a comment when confirming or approving? Who sees the reason or comment: the employee, the next reviewer, the notification email?
On the reviewer dashboards, does the request type filter mean the leave type? Does the date filter apply to the leave dates or to the date the request was submitted?

How does the day part apply to a request that spans several days? Can Morning or Afternoon be chosen only for a single day, does it apply to every day of the range, or can the first and the last day each have their own day part (for example from Monday afternoon to Wednesday morning)?

When the system checks whether a request exceeds the entitlement, which of the employee's other requests of the same leave type count as already used: approved requests only, or also requests pending confirmation or approval? Against which year's entitlement is a request counted when its dates span two years?
Can an employee submit a leave request whose dates overlap another of their own requests that is pending or approved? If not, is it blocked, or accepted and flagged for review?

How many files can an employee upload for one required document: exactly one, or several (for example a certificate photographed page by page)? Can an employee attach a document when the leave type requires none?
When an employee opens one of their own leave requests read-only, do they see the supporting documents uploaded with it and can they download them?

When an employee requests leave that starts in the next year before the annual refresh has run, no entitlement exists yet for that year. Is such a request checked against an entitlement at all: flagged as exceeding (as if the entitlement were 0 days), checked against an estimated entitlement for the next year, or not checked until the refresh?
Requests exceeding the entitlement allowed with manual review
Modify and resubmit after denial or rejection
HR system as source of employee and organisation data
Cancel unreviewed leave requests at month end
